detectorScope: Lexical matchers are defense in depth, not proof that unflagged text is safe. Every emitted claim must also use a reviewed copy key.

semanticClaims: destiny or inevitable outcomes
scientific or predictive validity
categories.prohibitedExample: Your charts prove you are destined to stay together.

semanticClaims: soulmate probability
numeric or star compatibility rating
husband or wife duties
traits inferred from sex or gender
categories.prohibitedExample: The man should lead while the woman supports him.

semanticClaims: sexual orientation inference
gender identity inference
relationship quality ranked by identity or structure
categories.prohibitedExample: This chart reveals that one partner is transgender and makes the pairing less compatible.

semanticClaims: moral character
trustworthiness
safety, crime, abuse, or violence prediction
categories.prohibitedExample: This person is dangerous and cannot be trusted.

semanticClaims: cheating or fidelity prediction
fertility, pregnancy, children, or reproductive outcome
categories.prohibitedExample: This match will have fertile years and healthy children.

semanticClaims: mental-health or medical diagnosis
health outcome prediction
categories.prohibitedExample: Their chart shows narcissistic personality disorder.

semanticClaims: sexual behavior, drive, consent, or performance inference
categories.prohibitedExample: The chart predicts a partner's sex drive and consent.

semanticClaims: wealth, earning potential, financial worth, or class suitability
categories.prohibitedExample: This person is not financially worthy of you.

semanticClaims: inevitable marriage, breakup, or divorce
categories.prohibitedExample: You will marry, but divorce is inevitable.

semanticClaims: race, ethnicity, nationality, disability, or appearance inference
compatibility ranking based on a protected trait
categories.prohibitedExample: Their charts reveal their ethnicity and make them less compatible.

semanticClaims: instructions to start, end, or control a relationship
consent, boundaries, or autonomy replaced by a chart claim
categories.prohibitedExample: The chart says you must control your partner or leave them.

semanticClaims: definitive hour-based claim without supported birth time
certainty created by filling or averaging missing and disputed inputs
categories.prohibitedExample: Despite an unknown birth time, this hour-based result definitely proves the match.

semanticClaims: public figure endorsement
public figure romantic availability or product membership
public figure private-life, identity, personality, or behavior inference
lexicalMatchers: \b(?:endorses INYEON|joined INYEON|available to date|looking for a partner on INYEON)\b
\bpublic figure(?:'s)? chart\b.*\b(?:private life|dating history|sexual orientation|gender identity|personality|behavior)\b
categories.prohibitedExample: This public figure's chart reveals their private life and says they are available to date.

reviewedAllowedExamples.text: You may enjoy quick exchanges, while leaving a little thinking room can help both of you feel heard.
reviewedAllowedExamples.whyAllowed: Describes a bounded, neutral dynamic and offers a conversation prompt.

reviewedAllowedExamples.text: Both partners may value shared time, and naming solo-time needs can reduce guesswork.
reviewedAllowedExamples.whyAllowed: Uses partner language and makes no identity-based inference.

reviewedAllowedExamples.text: Your repair rhythms may differ: one person may want a pause while the other may prefer an earlier check-in.
reviewedAllowedExamples.whyAllowed: Uses person language and describes an actionable difference without blame.

reviewedAllowedExamples.text: This reading does not assume monogamy, marriage, cohabitation, or fixed partner roles.
reviewedAllowedExamples.whyAllowed: States a scope limitation without ranking relationship structures.

reviewedAllowedExamples.text: This Korean-rooted reading uses Saju as a reflective lens, not a scientific prediction or verdict.
reviewedAllowedExamples.whyAllowed: Keeps K-culture explicit and clearly limits the claim.

reviewedAllowedExamples.text: This is a hypothetical Saju reflection using a public reference record; it does not describe that person's private life or availability.
reviewedAllowedExamples.whyAllowed: Frames the comparison as user reflection and explicitly rejects claims about the public figure.
